Subject: MedFin RFI: commercial terms for inference platform and consumption safeguards

Dylan,

Thanks for taking part in our RFI. Procurement and engineering asked us to get a clear read on commercial guardrails: per-token list price, commit/volume discounting, overage smoothing (true‑up cadence, burst protections), rollover credits, and any support credits tied to SLAs.

Specifically:
- We need a clear per-token baseline for text generation and embeddings (separate lines if you price differently).
- Describe three commit bands you would propose for a 12‑month contract (expected steady state ~1B tokens/mo, but with bursts to 1.8B).
- Explain overage handling: immediate billing vs monthly true‑up, smoothing windows, and whether you offer upfront buffer credits.
- Any language around rate changes, minimums, or protected volumes during audits?

Please keep the initial response high level with a short worksheet we can drop into our procurement packet.

Appreciate a reply by end of week — our demo is scheduled for next Wednesday.

Best,
Alice Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing
MedFin Inc.

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level answers below; Marissa (commercial) and Neha (security/compliance) are looped in for the spreadsheet and any controls language you need.

Per-token baseline (public list):
- Text generation: $0.0009 / 1K tokens (standard model family)
- Embeddings: $0.0015 / 1K tokens

Commit bands (12‑month):
1) Band A (Base) 200M tokens/month — 5% discount off list
2) Band B (Growth) 600M tokens/month — 18% discount off list
3) Band C (Enterprise) 1.2B+ tokens/month — 30% discount off list

Overage handling options we offer (pick one per contract):
- Monthly true‑up: usage billed monthly; overages charged at contracted overage rate (bands prorated).
- Buffered cushion + quarterly true‑up: one month of buffer credits on initial term; quarterly reconciliation, overages billed quarterly.
- Smoothing protection: apply a 60‑day rolling smoothing window for invoiceable usage (helps absorb short spikes).

We can offer a one‑time starter credit equal to 5% of first quarter committed spend to absorb onboarding variability. Rate changes: pricing guaranteed for term; changes only at renewal unless both parties agree.

I'll ask Marissa to put these into an RFI worksheet and include a worked example for 1B steady tokens with 80% utilization and 180% burst month.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MedFin RFI: commercial terms — follow up on smoothing / audit language

Tom —

Quick bullets you can paste into your evaluation doc:

1) Smoothing math (60‑day rolling window): a spike in month T increases total invoiceable tokens by the portion of the spike that exceeds the rolling baseline. Practically we calculate a 60‑day moving average for each customer; the delta between actual tokens and the moving average is amortized linearly over the 60 days. Example: 1.0B baseline, single month spike to 1.8B -> additional 0.8B tokens amortized: 0.8B / 60 days = ~13.33M tokens/day, invoiced proportionally across the next two months. This typically reduces immediate overage impact by ~70–80% depending on burst shape.

2) Protected minimum for initial onboarding: we offer a 90‑day protected period where committed volumes are prorated and not subject to downward adjustments for utilization drops caused by onboarding. That protection requires a standard onboarding plan and a single onboarding call every 30 days to review usage cadence.

3) Contracted overage rate: for clarity we propose a tiered approach — overage billed at the next lower band’s contracted rate plus a 10% premium (e.g., if you are in Band B contracted pricing and exceed into Band C for a short spike, overage units billed at Band C rate + 10% for that spike), or you can elect a flat multiplier (1.25x list) as a simpler rule. We'll state the chosen method in the commercial appendix.

Additional notes:
- Starter credit: 5% of Q1 committed spend applied as token credits on the first invoice.
- SLA credit: if latency SLOs are not met for two consecutive weeks, we provide a one‑time invoice credit equal to 2% of monthly committed spend; enterprise SLA language is negotiable.

- Marissa will finalize the RFI worksheet to reflect the smoothing math and protected minimum.
- If MedFin picks the smoothing + 1 month buffer option we can provide a draft commercial appendix and LOI by Friday.
